insights.summary: Trident Lifeline held no earnings call; this is from its H2 FY26 presentation (9 May 2026), which reports standalone numbers. FY26 standalone revenue crossed ₹100 Cr for the first time (₹106 Cr, +50%) with PAT of ₹18 Cr and a 27% EBITDA margin; H2 alone was ₹58 Cr (+47%), with domestic business the main driver. The company exports formulations under its own registrations (1,091 approved, 2,534 pending in 46 countries) using its own and contract plants, and plans 300-400 new registrations a year, but gives no numeric FY27 guidance beyond a 'robust' outlook.

what_changed.text: FY26 standalone revenue above ₹100 Cr (₹106 Cr)
Domestic share rose to 49% of standalone revenue in FY26 (30% in FY25)

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: With ongoing projects at the standalone and subsidiary levels, and operational strategies coming to fruition, the Company has established a foundation for continued growth.

red_flags.text: No earnings call; presentation gives standalone figures only, while most growth sits in subsidiaries.
Standalone receivables more than doubled to ₹49 Cr (from ₹20 Cr) on 50% revenue growth.
Free cash flow negative: ₹8 Cr operating cash flow against ₹20 Cr of investment in FY26.
EBITDA margin slipped to 27% from 29% in FY25.

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Pharma formulations (tablets 67% and capsules 30% of standalone revenue; syrups, suspensions, ointments), plus injectables, medical devices, herbal and cosmetics through subsidiaries
business_snapshot.customers: Distributors and B2B partners in Africa, Latin America, CIS and East Asia; domestic tenders and contract manufacturing
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26 standalone: domestic 49%, exports 51%; by region Asia ~57%, Africa ~25%, South America ~17%
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Export product registrations, off-patent molecules, emerging-market generics demand
